newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures end slightly higher in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures end slightly higher in Tokyo.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended higher on Thursday, supported by the Finance Ministry's (MOF) outright bond purchases this morning.
"There was some concern about what would happen to the MOF's outright bond purchases if they did not take place today," a trust bank trader said.
But the outright bond buying by the ministry this morning reassured the market, the trader said.
Most people in the market now probably expect the MOF's Trust Fund Bureau to continue making outright bond purchases for the time being, the trader added.
The market had been keen to know whether the bureau would extend its plan beyond December.
The official said that the JGB purchases were aimed at efficient and diverse portfolio management and that there were no policy implications.
"The JGB buying is not a measure to prop up the market and the bureau has not attached any policy implications to it," the official said.
The December ended at 124.45, up slightly from Wednesday's 124.34.
A city bank trader said the December was capped on the upside due to a rise in interest rate swap (IRS) rates.
Since the rise in JGBs in recent days was driven by a decline in IRS rates, a rise in IRS rates on Thursday has kept JGBs heavy on the upside, the trader said
The three-year IRS rate, which had shown the sharpest decline since Tuesday, rose during the day, and was quoted at 1.32/1.36 percent as of 0730 GMT, up from 1.27/1.31 percent on Wednesday.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.650 percent as of 0731 GMT, up from the previous day's 2.645 percent.
There was talk in the market that pension funds were buying long-term JGBs and selling medium-term JGBs, the first trader said.

Various financial institutions were detected changing the duration of the bonds in their portfolios, but there was little direct impact on the market as a result of such trades, the second trader said.
